# S147 — Keep an unset short title in step when set changes the title

`set ID --title "New"` updates the title but leaves `short_title` at the old text, even when the short title was never set separately. So `list` and the ROADMAP row keep showing the old title while the slice H1 shows the new one.

**Findings:** dogfooding S144: set --title left the old short_title, so list and ROADMAP kept the old title · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** re-syncing short titles that already drifted; changing how the ROADMAP chooses between title and short title; the slice H1.

## Why

Hit while re-titling S144. After `set S144 --title …` the index held the new `title` but `short_title` was still "Let a retired item depend on a retired item". `list` showed the old title until a separate `set --short-title`. Nothing warned that the two now disagreed.

`add` defaults `short_title` to the title (`ops.py:142`). `set_fields_many` (`ops.py:374`) sets each requested field independently, so `--title` alone never touches `short_title`. The `_sync_slice` docstring (`ops.py:340`) says the two differ on purpose, which is right when someone chose a short title. When `short_title == title` before the change, though, nobody chose one: it is only the default, and it should follow.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ops.py` (`set_fields_many`)
- tests covering `set` (for example `tests/test_cli.py`)
- `docs/agents.md` or `set --help` text if either describes `--title`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

## Failing tests

1. When an item's `short_title` equals its `title`, `set ID --title New` makes both "New", and `list` and the rendered ROADMAP row show "New".
2. When an item has a distinct short title, `set ID --title New` leaves the short title unchanged.
3. `set ID --title New --short-title Short` sets exactly those two values.
4. A multi-id `set` applies the rule to each item separately.
5. The log note records the short-title change along with the title change.
6. The TUI title edit, which goes through the same op, follows the same rule.

## Implement

In `set_fields_many`, when `title` is being set, `short_title` is not in the request, and the item's current `short_title` equals its current `title`, also set `short_title` to the new title. Do it before the change list is built, so the log shows it.

## Check

The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check` and `git diff --check`.
